title: Clinical Rotation Iii
description: This course is the third in the series of hospital rotations, emphasizing the practical application of respiratory care theory in monitoring neonatal, pediatric, and adult intensive care unit patients. Students will further develop the skills gained in RSPT 70A and 70B. Intended for students in the Respiratory Therapy Program; enrollment is limited to students accepted in the program.
outcomes: Evaluate and apply advanced diagnostic data to respiratory therapy techniques and the patient's illness.
Perform respiratory therapy techniques relating to the management of neonate, pediatric, and adult intensive care unit patients.
objectives: Demonstrate the correct technique for performing patient assessments.
Monitor and interpret hemodynamic data accurately.
Monitor parameters on mechanical ventilators accurately.
Demonstrate effective management of a minimum of three patients on mechanical ventilators.
Demonstrate effective ventilator weaning techniques and airway care.
Demonstrate effective management of patients on CPAP devices.
Demonstrate understanding of pathophysiology for adult and neonatal critical care.
Successfully observe and provide assistance with special procedures.
Recommend appropriate therapies for ventilator patients.
Evaluate effects of ICU respiratory therapy procedures.
Provide correct documentation of observations and therapies.
Demonstrate effective and appropriate communication skills with patients, family members, and hospital staff.
content: Management of patients on mechanical ventilators
Management of patients on CPAP devices
Pathophysiology for neonatal and pediatric critical care
Observation of and assistance with special procedures
Patient care plans and education with the patient/family members
lab: Management of patients on CPAP devices
Pathophysiology for neonatal and pediatric critical care
Observation of and assistance with special procedures
Communication with patients, hospital staff, patient's family members
